title: Prakas on Dispute Resolution in Securities Sector
text:
PRAKAS
ON
DISPUTE RESOLUTION IN SECURITIES SECTOR
SENIOR MINISTER, MINISTRY OF ECONOMY AND FINANCE
AS CHAIRMAN OF SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION
OF CAMBODIA
- Having seen the Constitution of the Kingdom of Cambodia;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kret No. NS/RKT/0913/903 of September 24, 2013 on the
Appointment of the Royal Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kret No.NS/RKT/1213/1393 of December 21, 2013 on
Adjustment and Fulfillment of Member of the Royal Government of the Kingdom of
Cambodia;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kret No.NS/RKT/0416/368 of on April 4, 2016 on
Adjustment and Fulfillment of Member of the Royal Government of the Kingdom of
Cambodia;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No.02/NS/94 of July 20, 1994 promulgating the Law on
the Organizing and Functioning of the Council of Ministers;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No. NS/RKM /0196/18 of January 24, 1996
promulgating the Law on the established Ministy of Economics and Finance;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No.NS/RKM/0107/001 of January 10, 2007
promulgating the Law on the Government Securities;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No.NS/RKM/1007/028 of October 19, 2007
promulgating the Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities;
- Having seen Anukret No.97 ANK/BK of July 23, 2008 promulgating the Law on
Organizing and Functioning of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Cambodia;
- Having seen the Anukret No.54/ANKR/BK of April 8, 2009 on the Implementation of the
Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities;
- In accordance with the approval made by the Securities and Exchange Commission of
Cambodia in plenary meeting on August 22, 2017;

HEREBY DECIDES
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
ARTICLE 1.-
The purpose of this Prakas is to prescribe medication and adjudication in securities sector
which are conducted by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Cambodia (SECC) in
accordance with the Law on Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities.
ARTICLE 2.-
Technical terms used in this Prakas are defined in this article and are available in the
glossary of the annex of the Law on Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities and that
of the Anukret on the Implementation of the Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-government
securities:
- “Law” refers to the Law on Issuance and Trading of Non-Government;
- “Anukret” refers to the Anukret on the Implementation of the Law on Issuance and
Trading of Non-Government Securities;
- “Complaint” refers to complaint for mediation or adjudication in accordance with this
Parkas;
- “Disputing Party/Parties” refers to any disputing party or both disputing parties;
- “Dispute or Dispute in Securities Sector” refers to all claims, disputes or controversy
involving securities or service in securities sector;
- “Arbitration Tribunal” refers to a sole arbitrator, or a panel of arbitrators, registered
with the National Commercial Arbitration Centre or outside that list. The list of arbitrators who
have been trained about securities sector by the SECC shall be published on website of the SECC
and/or other public media;
- “Mediator” refers to official of the SECC who is appointed to mediate any dispute
related to securities sector;
- “Adjudicator” refers to official of the SECC who is appointed by the Director General
of the SECC to adjudicate on any dispute related to securities sector.
CHAPTER II
COMPLAINT FOR MEDIATION
ARTICLE 3.-
A disputing party may file a complaint for mediation with the SECC through Department
of Legal Affairs of the SECC.
ARTICLE 4.-
A complainant or complainant’s representative shall have capacity to sue pursuant to the
Laws and the Civil Code of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

ARTICLE 5.-
A complaint for mediation shall contain at least the following information:
1. Names and addresses of disputing parties.
2. Objective of the complaint and detail of the claim.
3. Details of the dispute/Facts attaching with related documents.
When it deems necessary, Department of Legal Affairs may require the complainant to
provide further information or document, accompanying with document translated into Khmer
language if the original document is in foreign language.
Department of Legal Affairs shall require the complainant to rectify any complaint which
doesn’t contain enough information or which is improper within 7 (seven) working days from the
date of the receipt of the rectification notice.
ARTICLE 6.-
A complaint shall be dismissed when:
1. it is not related to securities sector;
2. it doesn’t contain not enough information or is improper;
3. it is made by a person who doesn’t have capacity to sue or interest in the dispute;
4. it is related to a criminal case;
5. it has been settled or is being settled by an arbitration tribunal or a court; or
6. it is made while a limitation period of rights to sue has already expired.
In case of dismissal of the complaint, the Director General of the SECC shall notify this
decision to the complainant.
ARTICLE 7.-
When a complaint is fully completed and complied with the requirement as prescribed in
this Prakas, the Division in charge of Dispute Resolution of Department of Legal Affairs as a
Dispute Resolution Centre in securities sector shall contact the disputing parties and invite them
to sign a mediation agreement in a form as set by the Director General of the SECC.
Before commencing the adjudication, the disputing parties shall pay all fees as determined
in the Annex of this Prakas, including the administration and mediator fees, and a deposit to cover
all expenses eventually incurred in connection with the mediation. Unless the disputing parties
agree otherwise, all fees in mediation shall be borne equally by the disputing parties. However, in
the event that a complainant is an investor, all fees in mediation shall be borne solely by the other
disputing party who is a company licensed by the SECC.
CHAPTER III
DISPUTING PARTIES
ARTICLE 8.-
A disputing party has the rights to:
1. Present the facts and add additional important documents;
3
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

2. Make request and give comment during the procedure;
3. Request to bring in a translator if necessary;
4. Request, with proper reason, to delay the conduct of mediation or adjudication;
5. Request for a copy of the record of mediation results; and
6. Other rights as prescribed in this Prakas.
ARTICLE 9.-
A disputing party has the obligations to:
1. Participate in mediation and adjudication procedure with honesty, morality, and
appropriate attitude and comply with the Rule of mediation and adjudication;
2. Cooperate with mediator or adjudicator and other disputing party;
3. Implement all clauses as set in mediation or adjudication agreement; and
4. Carefully abide by all related provisions of this Prakas.
ARTICLE 10.-
A Complainant may withdraw the complaint or agree with other disputer party to
withdraw from the mediation or adjudication at any time by giving notice of withdrawal in writing
to the Director General of the SECC through the Division in charge of Dispute Resolution.
CHAPTER IV
MEDIATION
PART 1
MEDIATOR
ARTICLE 11.-
A mediator or a panel of mediators consisting of not more than three mediators is
appointed by the Director General of the SECC upon request of the Head of Division in charge of
Dispute Resolution.
ARTICLE 12. -
A mediator shall:
1. Make enquiries to disputing parties to identify the issues in dispute;
2. Determine the issues in dispute and a method of mediation to be used;
3. Facilitate peaceful negotiation between disputing parties;
4. Generate settlement options for disputing parties;
5. Motivate and encourage disputing parties to reach agreement;
6. Perform functions in accordance with the Code of Conduct and the Rules of mediation;
7. Perform other functions as prescribed in this Prakas and other relevant regulations.
ARTICLE 13.-
A Mediator is empowered to:
4
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

1. Set up meetings by conducting a joint meeting with all or separate meeting with each of
the disputing parties;
2. Gather information involving the dispute from disputing parties;
3. Request for the appointment of a translator or expert; and call for a presence of other
related person if necessary;
4. Delay mediation meeting in order to allow the disputing parties to consider any specific
request or to add information or other opinions if necessary; and
5. Have other powers as prescribed in this Prakas and other relevant regulations.
ARTICLE 14.-
A person is not eligible to be a mediator if the person:
1. is a current or former spouse of the disputing party;
2. is a relative of disputing party within fourth degree of consanguinity, or is/was a
relative of disputing party within third degree of affinity;
3. had or has been in dispute with disputing party in the court;
4. has personal interest in the dispute;
5. was a witness or a representative or an expert who had assisted the disputing party; or
6. had or has been in any situation likely to create an impression of bias or the presence of
conflict of interest.
The person who is appointed to be a mediator shall inform the Director General of the
SECC immediately through the Division in charge of Dispute Resolution of the presence of any
circumstance as set in the above paragraph 1.
ARTICLE 15.-
The Director General of the SECC may replace the mediator(s) upon request of the Head
of Division in charge of Dispute Resolution in any of the following circumstances where:
1. the mediator(s) requests to withdraw from the mediation for any of the reasons as stated
in paragraph 1 of the Article 14 of this Prakas;
2. a disputing parties requests to replace the mediator(s) for any of the reasons as stated in
paragraph 1 of the Article 14 of this Prakas; or
3. there is any circumstance as prescribed in paragraph 1 of the Article 14, or any event as
prescribed in point 1 of the Article 19 of this Prakas.
PART 2
PROCEDURE AND TERMINATION OF MEDIATION
ARTICLE 16.-
The mediator(s) shall invite the disputing parties, by a written invitation letter or by other
means of communication, to participate in the mediation on the date and in the place as set by the
mediator(s). If a disputing party is unable to attend the mediation meeting as schedule, the
mediator(s) shall make a second and further invitations if the mediator deems necessary.
5
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

ARTICLE 17.-
The mediation meetings shall be conducted in confidence. Only the mediator(s) and the
disputing parties shall be permitted to present during the meetings.
A translator and an expert may attend the mediation process if the mediator(s) deems
useful to facilitate the mediation process. In this case, the translator and expert shall sign
confidentiality agreement in a form as set by the Director General of the SECC.
The mediator(s) may conduct joint meetings with all or separate meetings with each of the
disputing parties by giving the each disputing party a reasonable time; and the mediator(s) shall
make a record. This record shall be signed by the mediator(s); and it shall also be singed or
fingerprinted by the disputing parties.
The mediation shall be conducted in Khmer unless the mediator(s) agrees to use other
language.
ARTICLE 18.-
If any disputing party is absent from the meetings twice consecutively during the
mediation process without any proper reason, the dispute is deemed unsettled.
ARTICLE 19.-
The mediation process will be interrupted or suspended when there has:
1. Withdrawal, replacement, incapacity or death of a mediator, with the exception of a
panel of the mediators when the remaining mediators can continue to act;
2. Incapacity or death of any disputing party;
3. Extinction of legal personality of legal person, which is a disputing party, by a merger;
4. Force majeure; or
5. Other circumstances that the Director General of the SECC deems to have impact on the
mediation process.
The duration of mediation as set in the Article 21 of this Prakas shall be interrupted or
suspended until the mediation is resumed.
ARTICLE 20.-
The mediation will terminate when:
1. the disputing parties reach a settlement of the dispute;
2. the disputing parties agree to withdraw from the mediation;
3. the complainant withdraws his/her complaint for mediation;
4. the disputing party(s) is absent twice or more from mediation meeting without proper
reason;
5. the mediator(s) and the disputing parties agree to terminate the mediation for the reason
that further proceeding will not resolve the dispute between the disputing parties;
6. the disputing party(s) seriously breaches any provision as prescribed in this Prakas; or
7. any of the disputing parties dies or the legal personality of a legal person(s) which is the
disputing party(s) is extinct and the deceased person has left no one to undertake the
rights or obligations of the parties involving the mediation.
6
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

ARTICLE 21.-
The mediation process shall be concluded within 90 (ninety) days from the date of the
appointment of the mediator(s) by the Director General of the SECC with the exception of:
1. any circumstance as prescribed in the Article 19 of this Prakas, or
2. the decisions of the Director General of the SECC upon request for the extension of
time from the mediator(s) or from the disputing parties’ agreement.
ARTICLE 22.-
Any agreement of disputing parties reached in presence of the mediator(s) shall be
effective for execution.
The disputing parities may agree to prepare by themselves another separate settlement
agreement in presence of the mediator(s) by including more clauses and conditions.
ARTICLE 23.-
Any disagreed issue in mediation is deemed unsettled. The mediator(s) shall make an
unsettle mediation record in which indicates the disagreed issue(s), reasons and other essential
relevant information. The unsettled mediation record shall be properly dated and signed by the
mediator(s); the copies of the record shall be provided to the disputing parties.
The disputing party(s) may file a complaint for adjudication with the SECC in accordance
with the provisions as set in the Chapter 5 of this Prakas, or refer the dispute to arbitration
tribunal, or appeal to competent court. Valid period to refer dispute to arbitration tribunal or to
appeal to the court shall be within 90 (ninety) days from the date of the receipt the unsettled
mediation record by disputing parties; otherwise the rights to refer the dispute or to appeal will
lose.
CHAPTER V
ADJUDICAION
PART 1
COMPLAINT FOR ADJUDICATION
ARTICLE 24.-
The disputing parties, who can’t reach settlement agreement as mentioned in the
provisions as set in the above Chapter 4, may file a complaint for adjudication with the SECC
through the Division in charge of Dispute Resolution.
ARTICLE 25.-
A complaint for adjudication shall be dismissed when:
1. the objective of the complaint involves a monetary claim;
2. the claim amount exceeds 400.000.000 (four hundred million) Riels unless the
disputing parties agree to reduce the claim amount to be equal or less than 400.000.000
(four hundred million) Riels;
7
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

3. the complaint has been or is being settled by an arbitration tribunal or a court; or
4. the complaint is made after 90 (ninety) days from the reception date of the unsettled
mediation record as prescribed in the Article 23 of this Prakas.
ARTICLE 26.-
Before commencing the adjudication, the disputing parties shall sign an adjudication
agreement in a form as set by the Director General of the SECC; the disputing parties shall also
pay all fees as determined in the Annex of this Prakas, including the administration and
adjudicator fees, and a deposit to cover all expenses eventually incurred in connection with the
adjudication.
All fees and deposit in adjudication process shall be equally born by disputing parties,
unless otherwise agreed by the disputing parties.
PART 2
ADJUDICATOR
ARTICLE 27.-
1 (one) adjudicator or 3 (three) adjudicators shall be appointed by the Director General of
the SECC upon request of the Head of Division in charge of Dispute Resolution. For the panel of
3 (three) adjudicators, the Director General of the SECC shall appoint 1 (one) adjudicator to be
head of the adjudicator’s panel. The mediator(s) may be appointed as the adjudicator(s) for the
same dispute that he/she used to mediate.
The Division in charge of Dispute Resolution shall inform the disputing parties about
name and any essential information related to adjudicator or panel of adjudicators.
ARTICLE 28.-
An adjudicator shall:
1. Set up adjudication conference;
2. Determine clearly the issues in dispute;
3. Facilitate the settlement between disputing parties;
4. Perform functions in accordance with the Code of Conduct and the Rules of adjudication;
5. Issue adjudication award; and
6. Perform other functions as prescribed in this Prakas and any relevant regulations.
ARTICLE 29.-
An adjudicator is empowered to:
1. Gather relevant documents and information from the mediation process;
2. Gather other relevant information if necessary;
3. Require the parties to bring in a translator and an expert if necessary; and
4. Have other powers as prescribed in this Parkas and any relevant regulations.
8
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

ARTICLE 30.-
A person is not eligible to act as an adjudicator, if he/she is in any circumstances as
prescribed in point 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Article 14 of this Prakas.
The appointed adjudicator(s) shall immediately inform the Director General of the SECC
and disputing parties through the Division in charge of Dispute Resolution of the presence of any
circumstance as prescribed in the above paragraph. Upon receipt of such disclosure or of the
information, the Director General of the SECC shall appoint another person(s) as adjudicator(s).
ARTICLE 31.-
In case there is a request to withdraw from adjudication by adjudicator(s) or a request to
replace adjudicator made by the disputing party(s) for the reason as stated in paragraph 1 of the
Article 30 of this Prakas, or other reason as prescribed in point 1 of Article 34 of this Prakas, the
Director General of the SECC shall appoint another person(s) as adjudicators upon request of the
Head of the Division in charge of Dispute Resolution and within 5 (Five) working days from the
date of decision of the replacement of adjudicator(s).
SECTION 3
ADJUDICATION PROCEDURE AND TERMINATION
ARTICLE 32.-
The adjudicator shall invite the disputing parties, by a written invitation letter or by other
means of communication, to participate in the adjudication conference on the date and in the place
as set by the adjudicator(s). If disputing party(s) is unable to attend the adjudication conference as
schedule, the adjudicator(s) may make a second invitation.
ARTICLE 33.-
The adjudication conferences shall be conducted in confidence. Only the adjudicator(s)
and the disputing parties shall be permitted to present during the conferences.
The adjudication shall be conducted in Khmer unless the adjudicator(s) agrees to use other
language.
The translator, expert, lawyer, witness and other related person may attend in the
adjudication process if the adjudicator(s) deems necessary by signing a confidentiality agreement
in a form as set by the Director General of the SECC.
ARTICLE 34.-
The adjudication process shall be interrupted or suspended when there has:
1. Withdrawal, replacement, incapacity or death of the adjudicator;
2. Other circumstance or event as set in point 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the Article 19 of this Prakas.
The duration adjudication as set in the Article 36 of this Prakas shall be interrupted or
suspended until adjudication is resumed.
9
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

ARTICLE 35.-
The adjudication shall be terminated when:
1. the adjudicator(s) issues an award on the dispute;
2. the disputing parties reached settlement prior to the issuance of adjudication award;
3. the disputing parties agree to withdraw from the adjudication;
4. the disputing party(s) seriously breaches any provision as prescribed in this Prakas; or
5. any of the disputing parties die or the legal personality of the legal person(s) which is
the disputing party(s) is extinct and the deceased person has left no one to undertake the rights or
obligations involving the adjudication.
ARTICLE 36.-
The adjudicator(s) shall conclude the adjudication within 45 (forty-five) working days
from the date of appointment of the adjudicator(s), with the exception of:
1. any events as prescribed in the Article 34 of this Prakas; or
2. the decision of the Director General of the SECC upon request for the extension of time
from the adjudicator(s) or the disputing parties’ agreement.
ARTICLE 37.-
The adjudicator(s) may issues an award based on:
1. the agreement of the disputing parities;
2. the reasonable ground, equity or best practice in secuities sector;
3. the laws and regulations applicable to the objective of the dispute.
ARTICLE 38.-
The adjudicator(s) shall issue an award in writing by indicating the following matters:
1. Identity of the disputing parties;
2. Facts and issues in the dispute;
3. Grounds for the decision;
4. Decision;
5. Fees and expenses, by indicating the proportion born by each disputing party;
6. Effective date of the award;
7. Date of issuance of the award; and
8. Signature of the adjudicator or the panel of adjudicators, and in case that any
adjudicator cannot sign the award, the remaining adjudicator(s) shall sign and make note of this
incident.
For the panel of adjudicators, the award shall be made by the majority of adjudicators.
ARTICLE 39.-
The adjudication award shall be sent to the disputing parties within 7 (seven) working
days from the date of issuance of the award.
10
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

The securities operators, securities firms, central counter parties, derivative brokers,
issuers, and other persons who are approved, licensed, accredited, and registered by the SECC
shall comply with adjudicator award.
Within 10 (ten) working days from the date of issuance of the award, the disputing party
which is an investor shall notify about his/her decision whether or not to abide by the award. In
case the investor accepts to abide by the award, the disputing parities shall sign or fingerprint the
Agreement in the present of the adjudicator(s) within 5 (five) working days from the date of the
notification of the decision of the investor.
ARTICLE 40.-
In case the disputing party which is an investor, does not accept to abide by the
adjudication award, the disputing party may refer the dispute to arbitration tribunal or appeal to a
competent court.
In case the securities operators, securities firms, central counter parties, derivative brokers,
issuers, and other persons who are approved, licensed, accredited, and registered by the SECC, do
not accept to abide by the adjudication award, they may appeal to a competent court in accordance
with the Article 46 of the Law.
CHAPTER VI
OTHER PROVSISIONS
ARTICLE 41.-
The securities operators, securities firms, central counter parties, derivative brokers,
issuers, and other persons who are approved, licensed, accredited, and registered by the SECC
shall mention dispute resolution clause in contract, client agreement or other agreement form in
business relations in securities sector.
ARTICLE 42.-
The disputing parties are deemed to receive invitation letter, notification letter, settled
record, unsettled record, award, or other related documents in mediation and adjudication process
if those letters deliver to them personally or to business address or to residence or postal address.
If none of these can be found after making a reasonable inquiry, the disputing parties are deemed
to have been received those letters in case it is sent via registered letter or other means of
communication.
ARTICLE 43.-
The mediator, adjudicator, disputing parties, translator, expert, lawyer and other related
person in mediation or adjudication shall keep confidential of all information, correspondence by
email, discussed matter, request, record and other related documents. Those matters and
documents shall not be disclosed, interpreted or published, by way of speaking, performing or by
any other means with the exception that:
11
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

1- there has agreement of the disputing parties;
2- the laws and regulations being in force require otherwise;
3- the identities of the disputing parties are not disclosed; and
4- the matters or document is used for researching or statistic purpose of the SECC and the
identity of the disputing parties are not disclosed.
ARTICLE 44.-
The officials of the SECC, mediator and adjudicator shall be liable for any suit or other
legal proceeding with respect to anything done or omitted to be done in implementing in good
faith their functions, duties and powers as prescribed in this Prakas and other regulations in force.
ARTICLE 45.-
The fees for translator and expert shall be borne by any disputing party who requests for
the services or shall be equally borne by the disputing parties if the services are required by the
mediator(s) or adjudicator(s) unless the disputing parties otherwise agree.
CHAPTER VII
PENALTIES
ARTICLE 46.-
If securities operators, securities firms, central counter parties, derivative brokers, issuers,
and other person that are approved, licensed, accredited, registered by the SECC do not
implement a settled record or adjudication award as prescribed in Article 39 of this Prakas or the
obligation as prescribed in the Article 43 of this Prakas will be subject to the SECC’s transitional
fine of not more than 200,000,000 (two hundred million) Riels and/or to administrative sanction
as the following:
1. a warning;
2. a correction order;
3. a limitation or restriction on the license, approval or accreditation; or
4. a suspension or revocation of license, approval or accreditation.
CHAPTER VIII
FINAL PROVISIONS
ARTICLE 47.-
The SECC may adopt guidelines in accordance with the Law, Anukret and this Prakas to
facilitate for understanding and compliance of this Prakas.
12
noitalsnarT
laiciffonU

ARTICLE 48.-
The Director General of the SECC, Director Departments of Legal Affairs, All
Departments and units of the SECC, securities operators, securities firms, central counter parties,
derivative brokers, issuers, and other related person shall implement this Prakas as from the
signing date.

ANNEX OF PRAKAS No 012/17 SECC/PrK
DATED on SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
ON
ADMINISTRATION FEES, DEPOSIT
AND
MEDIATOR AND ADJUDICATOR FEE
* * * * *
1. DEPOSIT FOR MEDIATION AND ADJUDICATION
After signing a mediation agreement, each disputing party shall deposit with the Division
in Charge of Dispute Resolution of the SECC the amount of 1,500,000 (one million five hundred
thousand) Riels for covering the expense made during the mediation process. The remain amount
after deducting all expenses made shall be refunded to the disputing parties not later than 14
(fourteen) working days from the date of receipt of the settlement record.
In case the disputing parties haven’t reached settlement and file a complaint for adjudication
with the SECC, each of them shall make deposit again with the Division in Charge of Dispute
Resolution of the SECC the amount of 1,500,000 (one million five hundred thousand) Riels for
covering the expense made during the adjudication process. The remain amount after deducting
all expenses made shall be refunded to the disputing parties not later than 14 (fourteen) working
days from the date of receipt of the adjudication award.
In case the deposit amount is not enough to cover all the expense, additional payment shall
be borne by the disputing parties.
2. ADMINISTRATION FEE FOR MEDIATION OR ADJUDICATION
Disputing parties shall pay administration fee for mediation or adjudication as following:

Less than 80,000,000 1,000,000
From 80,000,000 to 160,000,000 1,000,000 80,000,000
From 160,000,001 to 240,000,000 2,000,000 160,000,000
+ 1,25 % excess over
From 240,000,001 to 320,000,000 3,000,000 240,000,000
From 320,000,001 to 400,000,000 4,000,000 320,000,000
Ifthevalueindisputeexceeds400,000,000(fourhundredmillion)Riels,theadministration
fee shall be 6,500,000 (six million five hundred thousand) Riels.
